title: Vesper and the Bell
premise: When Casper Oyelaran returns to the family house to bury his twin sister Vesper, he discovers the body in the coffin has his face — and the mirrors in the house have begun lagging a second behind reality, showing a version of him that keeps doing things he hasn't done yet. The lag is the work of the Bell, an entity his grandmother bargained with decades ago: it keeps a family alive by singing one twin into the other, and the debt has come due. Casper must learn the Bell's song's forbidden last verse — the one that names the singer instead of the sung — without joining in, while his reflection grows more solid and more desperate to take his place. In the end Casper sings the verse aloud alone, unmaking the bargain, burying the true Vesper, and walking out of the house with a reflection that no longer moves when he does.
about_author: Dominic Ishikawa is the pen name of a former funeral home archivist from coastal Oregon who spent eleven years cataloguing unclaimed remains before turning to fiction. Their stories mine the quiet horror of paperwork, inheritance, and the things families agree never to say out loud.

chapters.title: The Return Address
chapters.summary: Casper arrives home for Vesper's funeral, POV his, first person documentary voice. He records the house's details obsessively, noting the coffin is already closed and the funeral director won't meet his eyes. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into unease as small wrongnesses accumulate — his mother calls him by Vesper's name and doesn't correct herself.

chapters.title: Viewing Hours
chapters.summary: Casper insists on an open casket; POV his. The body inside wears his face, down to the scar on his chin. His mother, Ada, goes white and says only 'it always chooses.' He documents everything in his notebook, hands shaking. Emotional beat: horror displacing grief — he came to bury a sister and is looking at his own corpse.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: That night Casper notices the hallway mirror reflects the room a beat late — his reflection lowers its hand after he does. He tests it with a stopwatch, logging the delay: exactly one second, then 1.2. POV his. Emotional beat: the scientist's coping mechanism cracking as the data refuses to stay benign.

chapters.title: Ada's Silence
chapters.summary: Casper confronts his mother; POV shifts to Ada in close third. She reveals fragments: her own twin brother 'went quiet' at nine, and their grandmother sang to the house every dusk. She begs Casper to leave before the wake. Emotional beat: a mother's love expressed as eviction, guilt braided through every evasion.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Room
chapters.summary: Locked since her death, the attic room yields to Casper; POV his. He finds hymnals with verses blacked out, a child's shoe that isn't Vesper's, and a ledger of names — pairs of twins, each with one name struck through. The last open page has both Oyelaran names written side by side. Emotional beat: dread of inheritance, the past reaching up.

chapters.title: The Wake
chapters.summary: Relatives fill the house; POV rotates briefly through cousin Nkechi, who remembers Vesper's 'imaginary friend' that sang. The mirrors lag for everyone now, and guests keep glancing at Casper as if he's standing where he isn't. Emotional beat: communal denial — everyone senses it, no one will name it, and Casper feels the family's loyalty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: What the Reflection Did
chapters.summary: Casper wakes to find mud on his boots he never walked in; POV his. The mirror-Casper has begun acting independently during the lag — and the actions bleed back. He catches his reflection smiling before he feels the smile. Emotional beat: identity eroding, the terror of being authored by something else.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Casper deciphers the grandmother's hymnal; POV his, intercut with her 1974 diary entries. The Bell's song has five verses; four bind a family to survival. The fifth is torn out of every copy. The diary warns: 'learn it, never lend it your voice.' Emotional beat: obsessive hope — knowledge as a lifeline he can't stop grasping.

chapters.title: The Bell in the Well
chapters.summary: Following sound at dusk, Casper finds the source: a drowned bell in the old well, audible only at twilight. POV his. When he leans over, the lag reverses — the reflection moves first. Emotional beat: vertigo and awe; the horror is beautiful, and that beauty is the trap.

chapters.title: Nkechi's Tape
chapters.summary: Cousin Nkechi gives Casper a cassette Vesper mailed a week before her death; POV Nkechi, then Casper listening. Vesper's voice on tape: 'It's not killing me, it's finishing me. Don't learn the fifth verse, Cas — or learn it better than it does.' Emotional beat: posthumous love as both warning and dare.

chapters.title: The Struck Names
chapters.summary: Casper cross-references the ledger with parish records; POV his, with Ada forced to help. Every generation, one twin vanishes from records and memory alike — including Ada's brother, whom she cannot remember at all until Casper says his name aloud and she weeps. Emotional beat: truth as violence; loyalty revealed as the mechanism of erasure.

chapters.title: Half a Heartbeat
chapters.summary: The lag reaches two seconds; Casper's reflection now speaks. POV alternates between Casper and the reflection's italicized voice. It claims to be Vesper, wearing his face because 'someone had to come back.' Emotional beat: unbearable ambiguity — is this his sister's ghost, the Bell's lure, or himself?

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: An elderly neighbor, Mrs. Okonkwo, recalls the 1974 night the Bell last rang; POV hers. She heard two children singing and only one stop. She gives Casper the torn fifth verse, kept in a Bible for fifty years, and refuses to touch it. Emotional beat: the cost of witness — she has carried this alone since childhood.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Casper memorizes the verse silently, writing it in mirror-script so his reflection can't read it; POV his. The house retaliates: doors open onto 1974, the well rings at noon, Ada begins humming the fourth verse in her sleep. Emotional beat: mounting siege — the house is a lung, and it is inhaling.

chapters.title: Ada's Confession
chapters.summary: Ada finally tells the whole truth; POV hers. She didn't lose Vesper to the Bell — she invited it, decades ago, to save Casper from the fever that should have killed him. The Bell accepted Vesper instead. Emotional beat: guilt detonating; love and betrayal shown as the same act.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Sung
chapters.summary: The reflection offers a bargain: let it take Casper's place in the world and 'Vesper' lives on in it; POV his. It weeps with his eyes. He nearly says yes. Emotional beat: the seduction of survival at any price — the book's thematic crux made flesh.

chapters.title: Vesper's Room
chapters.summary: Casper finally enters his sister's actual bedroom, untouched; POV his. He finds her real diary beneath the floorboards: she discovered the fifth verse too, and chose to sing the fourth to buy him time, knowing it would unmake her. Emotional beat: grief transfigured — his sister's loyalty was the truth he'd been refusing.

chapters.title: Dusk, the Well, the Bell
chapters.summary: Casper goes to the well at twilight with the verse; POV his. The Bell rises, and the house's dead twins stand in the water, including the face from the coffin. It begins the song and pulls him toward the fourth verse, his own mouth opening without permission. Emotional beat: terror at the body's betrayal — the song sings you.

chapters.title: The Fifth Verse
chapters.summary: Climax. As the Bell's chorus swells, Casper sings the fifth verse alone — the verse that names the singer, turning the song inward on the Bell itself. POV his and, for one page, the Bell's. The mirror-Casper shatters; the well goes silent; the house exhales fifty years of held breath. Emotional beat: sacrificial clarity — he survives by refusing to survive at the Bell's terms.

chapters.title: Two Coffins
chapters.summary: The funeral is redone; POV Ada. Two graves now: one for the stranger's body, one for Vesper, whose name the whole family can suddenly remember saying. Nkechi places the cassette in the earth. Emotional beat: mourning finally allowed to be ordinary, grief with a floor under it.

chapters.title: The Unreflected Man
chapters.summary: Epilogue, POV Casper. The house is sold; his mirrors show rooms, not him. He keeps documenting — a new notebook, a new prayer — and sometimes at dusk he hums four verses and stops, deliberately, on the breath before the fifth. Emotional beat: haunted peace; identity as a thing chosen daily, one unsung note at a time.

chapters.title: Coda: What the Well Keeps
chapters.summary: Final chapter, POV the house itself across decades. New family, new mirrors, all accurate. But the well remembers a bell, and on certain twilights a fifth verse waits at the bottom, patient, half-learned. Emotional beat: quiet, unresolved dread — survival was bought, not won, and debts keep their own ledger.
